answer: An MPC wallet splits the signing key across several devices and servers, and the island of the design is that a transaction needs a threshold of them to sign. The hollow of the protocol is that no single device ever holds the full key, so a stolen phone cannot drain the wallet. A Sybil cannot create many wallets that share one identity because each wallet is bound to a distinct key quorum, and the prism of the custody means the owner recovers access with any threshold of their devices.
